subject: Request: Temporary SLA carveout for overnight handover during migration
messages:
From: Daniel Park <dpark@streamline.ai>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Requesting temporary support SLA carveout for migration window

Hi Naomi,

Quick note from the ops team: we have a critical data migration scheduled for 2028-05-22 22:00 PDT -> 2028-05-23 04:00 PDT. During the migration we'll be routing heavy write traffic to a fallback cluster which will increase our error surface and spike alert volumes.

We'd like to request a temporary relaxation of strict P2 response expectations (normal P2 SLA 4h -> request to allow 8h for the migration window) and a pre-agreed on-call bridge pattern so we don't escalate P2s to P1 unnecessarily. We understand this is an exception and want the proper runbook, contact list, and a short addendum to the SLA.

Can Redwood confirm whether an exception can be granted and what the escalation path would look like? We'd prefer to limit any credits or penalties for this one-off maintenance.

Thanks,
Daniel
Head of Ops, Streamline AI
[Attachment: migration-plan-summary.pdf (pdf)]

From: naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Requesting temporary support SLA carveout for migration window

Team — forwarding Streamline's ask. TL;DR: one-night migration, want P2 window extended to 8h for the 6-hr maintenance window and an agreed on-call bridge so P2s do not cascade to P1. They also asked to avoid automatic credit triggers.

Required from us:
- Quick operational proposal (who covers, escalation tree)
- Draft SLA addendum (1 page)
- Confirmation on whether credits will be waived for this event

Ben — can you outline the suggested on-call bridge and a minimal runbook? Karthik — any infra/auto-fallback actions during migration we should require? Marissa — I'll loop in Customer Success for approvals and communication.

If we can turn around a short proposal today that Daniel can sign, we should be fine.

-Naomi
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SLA_Carveout_Proposal_Streamline_v1.pdf (pdf)]

From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 13:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Requesting temporary support SLA carveout for migration window

Thanks Naomi. Proposed operational stance for the window:

- Pre-migration (T-24h): on-call kickoff call including Streamline ops + Redwood on-call (pager).
- Migration window (22:00 - 04:00 PDT): designate a single P1 responder (Karthik to rotate) and a separate P2 bridge responder (Ben) who will triage P2s for up to 8 hours before auto-escalation. P2s that look like systemic failures will be immediately escalated to P1.
- Post-migration (T+2h): post-mortem bridge for 60m.

Escalation path (minimal):
1) P2 -> P2 bridge (Ben) within 30m of alert; bridge triages for impact.
2) If bridge deems incident critical or spread across >2 customers -> escalate to P1 responder (Karthik) immediately.
3) P1 responder engages product & engineering leads and opens SEV channel.

We can propose a 1-night addendum that specifies the exact window, named on-call contacts, and that automatic SLA credits will not be triggered provided the agreed bridge pattern is followed (i.e., we will reconcile any credit questions post-mortem).

I'll attach a quick CSV of the on-call roster and a sample runbook.

-ben
Ben Carter
Support Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: oncall-roster-may2028.csv (csv)]

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Requesting temporary support SLA carveout for migration window

Ben — that escalation tree looks good. A couple technical caveats:

- We should require Streamline to enable the fallback cluster with circuit breaker thresholds and provide us a short playbook of expected error types (timeouts vs 5xx). That will help the bridge triage quickly.
- We'll open a temporary elevated logging shard for their tenant for the 6-hour window to speed triage (cost covered by Streamline as per their request).
- I'll volunteer to be P1 for this night but will need an explicit backup (I'll nominate Priya as backup).

If we get the signed addendum tonight we can attach the roster and the expected alert signatures and then confirm the kickoff call T-24h.

-karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <dpark@streamline.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 May 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Requesting temporary support SLA carveout for migration window

Hi Daniel — thanks for the details and for proposing a tight window. Redwood can approve a one-time SLA addendum for the 2028-05-22 22:00 PDT -> 2028-05-23 04:00 PDT migration under the following conditions: 

1) Streamline provides the circuit-breaker thresholds and expected alert signatures by EOD 2028-05-19.
2) Streamline agrees to the on-call bridge pattern outlined below (Ben = P2 bridge, Karthik = P1 responder; backup: Priya N.).
3) No automatic SLA credits will trigger if the bridge pattern is followed; credits will be reconciled after the post-mortem if gaps are found.

We attached a one-page SLA addendum and the on-call roster — please sign and return via the HubSpot link below. Once signed we'll schedule the T-24h kickoff with attendees from both sides.

Link to sign: https://hubspot.company/record/HS-52389

If this looks good I can have Marissa draft the outbound comms language for your customers.

Best,
Naomi
Customer Success — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SLA_Carveout_Proposal_Streamline_v1.pdf (pdf); oncall-roster-may2028.csv (csv)]
